bull_case: Meta can absorb extraordinary AI capex and R&D because its core ad engine still grows at high rates. If infrastructure intensity peaks, owner FCF/share can reaccelerate while share count remains controlled.
bear_case: The 2026 AI buildout may be economically maintenance-like rather than high-return growth capex. FCF/share already fell in 2025 and Q2 2026 FCF nearly vanished, so high reinvestment could dilute returns without visible payback.
thesis: META has a long reinvestment runway but the current incremental return is not yet proven. FY2025 FCF/share fell despite strong revenue and operating-income growth, and H1 2026 capex plus R&D exceeded operating cash flow. This supports an 80 runway score but only 65 incremental-ROIC and 50 FCF/share-quality scores. The dilution veto remains cleared because diluted shares have declined rather than compounded upward.

evidence.claim: FY2025 operating cash flow was $115.80B and free cash flow $43.585B versus $52.103B in 2024, while diluted shares fell from 2.614B to 2.574B. FCF/share declined from about $19.93 to $16.93.
H1 2026 operating cash flow was $64.09B, property-and-equipment capex $49.11B and R&D $39.36B from the frozen financial pack, implying an internal reinvestment absorption ratio above 100%.

FY2025 revenue increased 22% and operating income increased 20%, while Q2 2026 revenue still grew 28%; the operating engine remains productive even as the marginal return on the newest AI infrastructure is not separately disclosed.
Q2 2026 operating cash flow was $31.86B but company-defined FCF was only $0.784B; full-year capex guidance was $130B-$145B.
Diluted weighted-average shares fell from 2.629B in 2023 to 2.614B in 2024 and 2.574B in 2025; Q2 2026 diluted shares were 2.566B versus 2.570B a year earlier.

counterevidence: The return on 2026-2030 AI infrastructure is not separately disclosed, so incremental ROIC cannot be measured cleanly.
FY2025 FCF/share fell about 15% despite strong revenue growth.
Q2 2026 FCF was only $0.784B because of the capex surge.
Reality Labs continued to lose roughly $19B annually, consuming reinvestment capacity outside the proven ad engine.
unknowns: Maintenance-like versus growth capex within AI infrastructure is not disclosed.
A clean incremental NOPAT/incremental invested-capital series for the 2025-2026 AI buildout is unavailable.
The timing of infrastructure utilization and corresponding revenue contribution is not sufficiently disclosed to calculate project-level ROIC.
falsifiers: Revenue continues growing double digits but owner FCF/share remains below the 2024 level through 2028.
Capex remains above $130B annually without a visible increase in incremental operating profit or cash conversion.
Diluted shares begin rising materially despite continued high SBC and buybacks remain uneconomic.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Diluted shares declined across 2023-2025 and were slightly lower YoY in Q2 2026. The long-duration excessive-dilution condition is false even though SBC is economically large.

Recent marginal returns are uncertain, but FY2025 revenue and operating income still grew 22% and 20%, and Q2 revenue grew 28%. Evidence does not establish ROIC below cost of capital on a structural basis.

key_kpis.name: Owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: exceed FY2024 level on normalized basis by 2028

key_kpis.name: Capex + R&D / OCF
key_kpis.threshold: decline from >100% while growth remains healthy

key_kpis.name: Incremental operating profit per incremental capital
key_kpis.threshold: clear evidence AI investment earns above cost of capital

next_checks: Rebuild TTM reinvestment absorption and owner FCF/share after Q3/Q4 2026.
Separate AI infrastructure maintenance and growth components if management provides enough disclosure.
Compare incremental FoA operating profit with cumulative AI capex to estimate realized ROIC.

subscores.rationale: Core economics remain strong, but the newest AI infrastructure return is not measurable. This is above the 50 uncertainty anchor because revenue/operating income continue to expand, but below the 75 'superior' anchor without clean marginal-return evidence.

Using the permitted H1 2026 fallback because a clean TTM series is not frozen, (capex + R&D)/OCF is about 138%, showing very high internal absorption. The >60%/90 row additionally requires incremental ROIC >=2x cost of capital, which is not established, so one lower observable band at 80 is used.

FCF/share fell from roughly $19.93 in 2024 to $16.93 in 2025 and was heavily compressed in H1 2026, but share count is declining and the distortion is plausibly investment-driven. This fits the 50 'distortion large' anchor rather than 25 structural decline.

uncertainties.rationale: Project-level returns on the AI buildout are not disclosed.
The runway is obvious, but the H1 fallback rather than exact TTM is used.
Normalization depends on whether current capex is temporary growth investment or a persistently higher maintenance burden.
